summary: This excerpt from 'Book 15 — part 48' is a fiction passage narrated around Ray, a sergeant (addressed as Gunny), and Lieutenant Holcomb, whose unit flies at night over the desert toward Karbala during a military operation involving Russoturk forces and allied bombing. The narrator contrasts the sergeant's role as the unit's entertainment and child-rearing overseer with the dismissive attitude of METOC staff toward the young lieutenant's mission. The scene is set in a low-flying helicopter with Ray, Holcomb, comm specialist Kev Whitfield and gunners, while a Predator follows by infrared, and the text ends mid-sentence as the pilot plans a flyover to clear the drop zone.
one_line: Fiction excerpt: a night helicopter run over the desert toward Karbala with Sergeant Ray and Lieutenant Holcomb ahead of a drop.
key_facts: Sergeants are described as the backbone of the military and also the entertainment directors of their units.
METOC personnel regarded the lieutenant's mission as a lark granted to a highly connected young officer with too much classical education and too much imagination.
Ray was ordered to help toughen up the lieutenant and show him what New Mes and the real world look like without getting killed.
The scene takes place around 2300 hours New Mes local time.
The helicopters fly at a height of ten meters, kicking up sand that stings the eyes and sticks in the teeth.
Ray, Lieutenant Holcomb, comm specialist Kev Whitfield and gunners manning the mini-guns ride in the lead chopper.
The rest of the team follows in a Predator, tracking the route by infrared imaging more than visual.
Kev Whitfield carries an M202 subby across his knees and is not happy about sitting on the bench with the LT.
East of the flight path are the scant, twinkling lights of Karbala.
The 8th Tactical Wing bombers are heard shouting toward industrial complexes on the city's fringes.
The Russoturk armored divisions are hunkered down to escape allied smart bombs.
Ray blames his parents for his tendency to fall asleep in helicopters, since they celebrated the American love of the open road during his colic-prone first two years.
The pilot tells Gunny that the helicopter is about a minute from the drop point and will flyover the zone, then hover three klicks east.
